newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms, short-dated swaps rise.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms, short-dated swaps rise.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar in late trading on Thursday, with operators focusing on short-dated swaps, dealers said.
They said operators' concern about liquidity conditions on Friday appeared to have triggered sharp fluctuations in short-dated swaps, pushing the tom/next rate to a high of 4.0 points.
They said the tom/next rate opened at around 1.6 points and quickly soared to 4.0 points at mid-morning. It eased to 3.25 points at midday before soaring again to the early high.
It was quoted at around 3.65 points at 0835 GMT.
"We don't know yet whether liquidity would be tight or not on Friday. But operators are getting nervous and they just keep covering," one Japanese bank dealer said.
He said the anticipated illiquid conditions haunted both offshore and local players because of the extremely tight rupiah supply on the past two Fridays.
Dealers said the situation might be worsened by the month-end factor and weekly tax payments due on Friday.
Liquidity on Thursday was ample, with overnight money last traded at nine percent, dealers said.
The Japanese bank dealer said the central bank had offered overnight paper (SBIs) at eight percent, which could help shift some liquidity away to Friday.
One local bank dealer said another indication of the general worry was that the tom/next rupiah deposit rate also had risen to 22 percent from 15.0/20.0 percent.

Dealers said spot dollars also came under light pressure due to liquidity concerns. But the U.S. bank dealer said an ongoing political dispute centred on ousted Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) leader Megawati Sukarnoputri appeared to have blocked operators from aggressive dollar selling.
A deadline for the closure of an office set up by Megawati was due to expire on Thursday but was later extended to Friday morning.

The East Jakarta municipality had ordered the office in a two-storey suburban area closed on the grounds that it violated residential zoning regulations. The office was set up after police evicted Megawati's supporters from the central PDI headquarters after she had been ousted as party leader.
Some dealers said operators were keeping a close watch on the situation because they feared it could lead to violence.
Spot rupiah was at 2,318.0/19.0 at 0905 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,319.0/20.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,314.25/15.00 and 2,316.00/16.75, respectively.
One-month swap was last at 16.00/17.25, two at 31.00/33.0, three at 47.50/49.00 and six at 95.00/96.00 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,314/2,506 and the conversion rate also by one point to 2,314/2,362 on Thursday.
